figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of our framework for studying how representation choice influences downstream learning and reconstruction. A pretrained diffusion model performs reverse diffusion using the ground-truth conditioning factor M to generate target latent variables zi, which are tokenized into Vi. The latent model maps neural activity onto tokenized latent representations, which are then untokenized into z′i. Simultaneously, the conditioning factor model predicts M ′ using the ground-truth conditioning factor M as the target. During inference, z′i and M ′ are injected into the pretrained diffusion model to reconstruct the target stimulus.

Fig. 2. Training dynamics for the conditioning factor and latent models. The top row shows training and validation losses and the bottom row shows validation Word Error Rate (WER) under teacher-forced generation. Although all models showed stable optimization, downstream reconstruction performance depended on the intermediate representation.
